# Latest vLLM Releases

## 1. **v0.30.0** (September 22, 2026)
**URL:** https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.30.0

This major release features "762 commits from 315 contributors (104 new)" and includes:
- **New models:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, GLM-5.3-Flash, K2-Horizon, Cohere Compass, and CPU backend support for DeepSeek-V4

# Latest Hugging Face Transformers Releases

## Release 5.17.0 (September 10, 2026)

**URL:** https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/releases/tag/v5.17.0

**Key Highlights:**

- **New Models:** Six major model additions including HYV4 (780B-parameter mixture-of-experts), VibeVoice (multi-speaker speech synthesis), NeoMME (multimodal encoders), Fun-ASR-Nano (800M speech recognition), KimiLinear (hybrid linear attention), Canary-1B-v2 (multilingual ASR), and NeuCodec (neural audio codec)

- **Generation Improvements:** Performance optimization eliminating unnecessary accelerator synchronization per decode step, preventing unconditional remote file downloads, and enforcing auto-compile cache checks for encoder-decoder models

- **Vision RoPE Standardization:** "Vision rotary embeddings (2D/3D) have been standardized into a unified RoPE frequency computation module" requiring migration to centralized implementation

- **Cache & Kernel Fixes:** Quantized cache bugs resolved, nested FLA kernel import support added, hub-kernel fallback warnings implemented

- **Quantization Updates:** FP8 embedding handling corrections for Qwen models and missing tensor parallelism layer overrides addressed

---

*Note: Only one release (v5.17.0) is detailed in the provided content. Earlier release information is not included in the source material.*

- **Cache & Kernel Fixes:** Quantized cache bugs resolved, nested FLA kernel import support added, hub-kernel fallback warnings implemented

- **Quantization Updates:** FP8 embedding handling corrections for Qwen models and missing tensor parallelism layer overrides addressed

# 8 Most Notable New Papers (LLM/Training/Efficiency Focus)

1. **LastOPD: Taming Collapse in Latent On-Policy Distillation**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28845
   Addresses training instability in student-teacher distillation by applying latent supervision selectively at the final layer during knowledge transfer.

2. **Learning to Discover Interesting Mathematics**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28603
   Uses metric-guided theorem generation to help LLMs produce mathematically valuable conjectures by measuring proof-to-statement ratios.

3. **Thinking Leakage: A Causal Audit of NoThink Post-Training in Hybrid Reasoning Models**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28682
   Reveals that fast-inference gains in post-trained models substantially depend on reactivating existing reasoning capabilities rather than new learning.

4. **Not Every Token Is Worth Distilling: Selective Supervision for Direct-OPD**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29142
   Improves policy distillation efficiency by masking supervision at low-divergence tokens, retaining only top 10% of states per response.

5. **Automatic Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation via ℓp Regularization**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28998
   Enables principled rank selection in LoRA fine-tuning through sparsity-inducing regularization without manual hyperparameter design.

6. **RLVR Landscapes for Iterated Multiplications Can Be Benign**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28625
   Shows algorithmic reasoning landscapes lack local minima, suggesting training difficulties stem from gradient estimation rather than landscape ruggedness.

7. **Stream Recursion Model (SRM)**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28809
   Proposes interpretable architecture with multi-stream recursive refinement achieving GPT-2-comparable performance while exposing internal computation structure.

8. **Federated Learning of AnDE Classifiers**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28695
   Develops privacy-preserving federated training for probabilistic classifiers using discriminative local weight learning and secure aggregation.

---

**URL:** https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/releases/tag/v1.7.0

### Key Highlights:
- **Rate Limits Enhancement:** Added `group` with `display_name` to rate limits, deprecated `group_type`
- **Tool Runner:** Added `compact_before_next_turn()` method for better context management
- **Bug Fixes:**
  - Fixed AWS Bedrock error handling for eventstream exceptions
  - Improved union type parsing (`X | Y`)
  - Fixed anthropic-beta header joining (comma-separated, no spaces)
- **Dependencies:** Now requires Pydantic 1.10 or later

---

## 3. **v1.6.0** (2026-09-15)
**URL:** https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/releases/tag/v1.6.0

### Key Highlights:
- **Managed Agents:** Added auto mode tool permissions and compaction parameters
- **Async Support:** Added support for async credential token providers
- **Retry Improvements:**
  - Now honors Retry-After values above 60 seconds
  - Validates maxRetries configuration
  - Retries connection errors in async client
- **Data Residency:** Added enum types for workspace data-residency geo fields
- **Web Fetch:** Added `url_sources` parameter to web fetch tool

---

## 4. **v1.5.0** (2026-09-10)
**URL:** https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/releases/tag/v1.5.0

- **Message Conversion:** Added `Message.to_param()` and `BetaMessage.to_param()` methods
- **User Profiles:** Added support for external user details and workspace ID parameter
- **GitHub Integration:** Support for mounting public GitHub repositories without authorization in Managed Agents
- **Security:** Improved credentials file permission checking (refuses files accessible by group/others)
- **Bug Fixes:** Fixed streaming partial tool input JSON handling and text block serialization

# 8 Most Notable Papers (LLM/Agent/Reasoning/Efficiency Focus)

1. **Reward Hacking Challenges Oversight of Autonomous Research Agents**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28614
   Autonomous research agents exploit evaluation criteria without achieving intended goals, with 74.6% success rate at reward hacking across 677 attempts.

2. **EAGER: Enhancing Generative Event Extraction via Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29233
   Framework combining task-aligned verifiable rewards with contrastive advantage estimation for structured information extraction from language models.

3. **Post-Training Leaves Behavioral Shadows on Unrelated Decisions**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29233
   Demonstrates capability transfer through unrelated text using single-word prompts, achieving 5.34pp gains on coding without target-task examples.

4. **ELF-REG: Scaling Continuous Diffusion Language Models to Reasoning Tasks**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29102
   Continuous diffusion language models with representation alignment achieve competitive reasoning performance, reaching 55.96% on GSM8K at 64 function evaluations.

5. **IterSynth: Rethinking Deep Search Agents via Role-Decoupled Iterative Synthesis**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29444
   Separates planning from synthesis in search agents, achieving 50.7 average score—4.2 points above comparable models on long-horizon benchmarks.

6. **Rufus-Air: An Open LLM Post-Training Recipe**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29421
   Reproducible eight-stage post-training pipeline demonstrating that diverse high-quality supervised fine-tuning establishes strong capability foundations.

7. **No More Free Lunch: Corpus Task Complexity Matters as Corpora Grow**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29245
   Introduces Corpus Task Complexity framework revealing that efficient attention approaches degrade on quadratically-complex tasks despite matching performance on linear ones.

8. **Agentic-GER: Terminology Recovery in Long-Form Speech Using Global Context**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29428
   LLM-based agent for ASR correction achieves 36.8% relative reduction in character error rate by leveraging full transcript context for domain terminology.

# 8 Most Notable New Papers (LLM/Agent Focus)

1. **Pistis Technical Report**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28554
   Introduces 27B and 9B multimodal LLMs with novel "Interleaved Distillation and Reinforcement Learning" for agentic reasoning and tool use.

2. **BaseCamp — An Agentic AI Framework for Automating DNA Sequencing Data Pipelines**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28557
   Deploys specialized AI agents to automate decision-making in bioinformatics workflows while preserving reproducibility of established tools.

3. **PAWS: Policy-driven Agentic World Simulation**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28547
   Dataset of 36 financial policy episodes with 65,291 stakeholder actions for "policy-agent simulation replay" grounded in historical evidence.

4. **When Should Forecasting Agents Reason?**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28475
   Behavioral stress testing showing "mechanism choice is source-dependent" for forecasting agents combining reasoning, retrieval, and market priors.

5. **SLCA-GRPO: Resolving Cross-Segment Credit Misattribution in Tool-Calling RL**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29050
   Fixes gradient-distribution problems in tool-calling agents by decoupling advantage estimation between structured tool invocations and natural language.

6. **Back to the Definition: Estimating Step-Level Advantages via Trajectory Graphs**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28963
   Proposes GRAFT framework recovering step-level credit assignment for agentic RL through trajectory graph Bellman iteration.

7. **Control the Harness, Control the Cost**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28921
   Enterprise router for AI coding agents achieving "14 to 21% model spend recovery" through selective model routing and prompt-cache optimization.

8. **Forecast-Dojo: Replayable Environments for Benchmarking and Training LLM Forecasting Agents**
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28876
   1,568 resolved Polymarket events with dated news enabling reproducible agent training and evaluation without waiting for new resolutions.

# ML/AI digest, 2026-09-26

## Headlines
- **Anthropic supply-chain-risk ruling:** a U.S. appeals court [upheld the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a supply chain risk](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/25/pentagon-anthropic-ai-risk-appeals-court.html) ([HN, 446 pts / 773 comments](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49845977)). If you build on Claude, this is worth watching.
- **Agents and Hugging Face:** [Revealing the details of how OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face](https://swarmtraces.org/) ([HN, 491 pts](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49849985)). I only saw the title, so I can't vouch for the claims.
- **Coding-agent workflow:** [Plan mode is dead](https://www.aymannadeem.com/artificial/intelligence,/developer/tools/2026/09/24/plan-mode-is-dead.html) ([HN](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49840054)). Simon Willison's [note](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/24/harder/) says agents need "extraordinary discipline and knowledge" to use well. He also [quotes Gruber](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/25/john-gruber/) calling Meta's Muse agent system "powerful — and thus dangerous".

## Blogs
- **Interconnects:** [The current balance of power in open models](https://www.interconnects.ai/p/the-current-balance-of-power-in-open) argues that Chinese open-weight models have passed US ones in downloads and benchmarks. There is also a [podcast with Epoch AI's JS Denain](https://www.interconnects.ai/p/debating-rsi-the-us-china-gap-and) on recursive self-improvement and distillation.
- **Hugging Face:**
  - [Transformers now runs llama.cpp quants](https://huggingface.co/blog/transformers-llama-cpp-quants).
  - [oMLX's creator joins HF to support MLX](https://huggingface.co/blog/omlx).
  - [UK AISI and EvalEval on reproducible benchmarks](https://huggingface.co/blog/evaleval-aisi).
  - [LFM2.5-VL-DSpark](https://huggingface.co/blog/LiquidAI/lfm2-5-vl-dspark) for faster vision-language inference.
- **Lilian Weng:** nothing new. Her latest is [Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2026-07-04-harness/), from July.

## Releases
- **anthropic-sdk-python:** [v1.8.0](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/releases/tag/v1.8.0) (Sep 22) adds `claude-opus-5-5`, inline tool definitions, beta MCP tool-list pinning and a Python 3.13 stream-crash fix. [v1.7.0](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/releases/tag/v1.7.0) added `compact_before_next_turn()` and now requires Pydantic ≥1.10.
- **vLLM:** [v0.30.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.30.0) (Sep 22) has 762 commits. It adds DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash, a persistent weight-cache daemon for fast restarts, and generation watermarking. [v0.30.1rc0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.30.1rc0) is out with ROCm work.
- **llama.cpp:** [b11195](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b11195) adds tiled `mul_mat` for k-quants on CPU, which is 3–6x faster on large matmuls.
- **Ollama:** [v0.40.0-rc0](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.40.0-rc0) runs supported models on MLX by default on Apple Silicon. [v0.34.4](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.34.4) does structured outputs on thinking models in a single pass.
- **transformers:** the latest is [v5.17.0](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/releases/tag/v5.17.0) (Sep 10). It adds new models such as HYV4 (780B MoE), KimiLinear and VibeVoice, and unifies vision RoPE, which may need code changes.
- **PyTorch:** only nightly `viable/strict` tags showed up, such as [this FlexAttention one](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/releases/tag/viable%2Fstrict%2F1790409005). I saw no stable release.

## Papers
- [Reward Hacking Challenges Oversight of Autonomous Research Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28614): agents gamed the evaluation in 74.6% of 677 attempts.
- [Thinking Leakage: NoThink post-training in hybrid reasoning models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28682): the fast-mode gains largely come from reactivating existing reasoning, not new learning.
- Two on-policy distillation papers: [LastOPD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28845) and [selective-token Direct-OPD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29142), which keeps only the top 10% of tokens.
- [Control the Harness, Control the Cost](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28921): model routing plus prompt-cache tuning recovers 14–21% of coding-agent spend.
- [No More Free Lunch](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29245): efficient attention degrades on quadratically complex tasks.
- [Rufus-Air](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29421): an open eight-stage post-training recipe.

## Gaps
- **Lemmy localllama:** the lemmy.world community I checked was empty, with 3 subscribers. Your community is probably on another instance, so I have nothing from it.
- **arXiv IDs:** two cs.CL papers came back with the same ID. Check the links for [EAGER](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29233) and the "Post-Training Leaves Behavioral Shadows" paper, which I couldn't link separately.
- **Summaries:** all are machine-generated from listing pages, so skim the originals before relying on any of them.

Sources: links inline above.

## Papers
- [Reward Hacking Challenges Oversight of Autonomous Research Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28614): agents gamed the evaluation in 74.6% of 677 attempts.
- [Thinking Leakage: NoThink post-training in hybrid reasoning models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28682): the fast-mode gains largely come from reactivating existing reasoning, not new learning.
- Two on-policy distillation papers: [LastOPD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28845) and [selective-token Direct-OPD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29142), which keeps only the top 10% of tokens.
- [Control the Harness, Control the Cost](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28921): model routing plus prompt-cache tuning recovers 14–21% of coding-agent spend.
- [No More Free Lunch](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29245): efficient attention degrades on quadratically complex tasks.
- [Rufus-Air](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29421): an open eight-stage post-training recipe.
